text_to_speech: Women and children are turned away from domestic violence refuges every week due to a lack of space. Domestic violence is the leading cause of homelessness among women. Given these well known issues, will your homelessness task force have any focus on those fleeing domestic violence and what are your target outcomes relating to domestic violence and homelessness? What are your tangible outcomes? Ok, so, on the general point first, of the task force, I’m extremely pleased with the progress we are making. You probably saw the really big breakthrough in the budget was that we were allocated new money on top of what councils currently have for launching what we call the ‘Housing First’ pilot, and that will be an opportunity for those who are currently rough sleeping to move into accommodation and then rebuild their lives from that. So that was a clear, tangible outcome that we definitely would not have got previously. There will also be new news, this Friday, and I take an opportunity just to sort of flag this. We’ll be launching a scheme that we call Alternative Giving. It’s launching in Birmingham first (I remember you saying you were a Birmingham resident, not a Sandwell resident) to enable people to contribute to all the homeless charities that have come together so people might feel that they don’t want to give to people on the street because it’s never quite clear how money will be used. That’s something very tangible there as well. On the particular part of your question, we have broken the task force down into different groups, so some looking at young people, some looking at single, mature people who tend to be male, but particularly also looking at that family and children’s piece and the domestic violence piece is part of that work. What I can say to you today is yes it’s definitely [inaudible], especially within the terms of reference. However, have we got an outcome of that yet? No, we have not. But very clearly the way it’s been constructed is trying to look at the different groups and the different issues that are in there. What has clearly got to happen is we, in terms of an outcome, we have got to find more refuge space because that’s what I am told, by things like the Amirah Foundation in Sparkbrook, is just not sufficient. But can I say today we’ve actually achieved that? No, we haven’t, but we’ve got the right people looking at it. Yeah, sorry, I should say to everybody in how we deal with this. You're quite welcome to come back once, twice, but we do need to move on to other questions in time but I don't mind you coming back. Or, I'll say one more thing, if you wanna help me understand something, you're very welcome to do that as well. I suppose I’d be interested to know when we can expect to hear a tangible outcome, when you might come forward and say, "We want to increase refuge spaces by so much, by this time" I think the fair answer is probably about March; thinking about the timeline of the homelessness task force that’s been set up so I don’t mind saying that. Okay Thank you
